function.name: calculate_electric_current
function.description: Calculate the electric current through a conductor given voltage and resistance. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

voltage.description: The voltage across the conductor in Volts. This is a float type value.

resistance.description: The resistance of the conductor in Ohms. This is a float type value.

conductance.description: The conductance of the conductor in Siemens. Optional if resistance is provided. Default: 0.3 This is a float type value.

message.content:
Electricity wasn’t “discovered” by a single individual—rather, its nature unfolded gradually through contributions from many thinkers and experimenters over millennia: | Era | Key Contributors | Major Contributions | |-----|------------------|----------------------| | **Ancient Greece** | *Thales of Miletus* (~600 BCE) | Noted static attraction when rubbing amber (“electrum”). | | **17th–18th Century** | *William Gilbert* (1544‑1603) – coined the term *electricus*.
*Benjamin Franklin* (1706‑1790) – proposed positive/negative charges, invented the lightning rod. | Early systematic study of electrical phenomena. | | **Late 18th Century** | *Alessandro Volta* (1745‑1827) – created the first chemical battery (the voltaic pile). | Demonstrated continuous electric current. | | **Early 19th Century** | *Michael Faraday* (1791‑1867) – discovered electromagnetic induction. | Laid groundwork for generators & motors. | | **Mid‑19th Century** | *James Clerk Maxwell* (1831‑1879) – unified electromagnetism into equations. | Provided theoretical framework linking electricity and magnetism. | So while there isn’t a single “discoverer,” the cumulative work of these pioneers—and countless others—led us to understand and harness electricity today.
